non_blocking_notes.issue: CI dependencies pytest, jsonschema, and PyYAML are installed without pinned versions or a lockfile.
non_blocking_notes.impact: Future upstream package changes could alter CI behavior without a repository change and reduce reproducibility.
non_blocking_notes.recommended_action: Consider pinning CI dependency versions or using a lockfile or hash-checked requirements file in a follow-up change.

tests_missing: An actual Azure DevOps pipeline execution against this exact commit was not part of the manual Gemini review.
reasoning_summary: Independent read-only review of exact commit 514217e474e46872c12efdad181d11ae90bfe57e found the change limited to the Azure Pipelines dependency-install step. The commit adds jsonschema and PyYAML alongside pytest so the CI test suite can import dependencies used by repository tests and core modules. Local validation reported 390 passing tests and 1 skipped test. No blocking correctness, security, authority-boundary, or safety issues were identified. The only material residual concern is the pre-existing use of unpinned CI dependencies.
proposed_rules: CI test dependencies should preferably be version-pinned or supplied through a reproducible lockfile or hash-checked requirements file, applied consistently across Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions.
